auxiliary_material: The authors observed that nucleotide levels in PBMCs were significantly higher than in RBCs (10, 55, and 5.6 fold for ATP, GTP, and ITP, respectively), attributing this to de novo synthesis in nucleated cells versus salvage pathways in RBCs. The study noted that plasma contamination is minimized by the strong ion exchange step since nucleotides are primarily intracellular and extracellular purines exist mainly in parent forms due to phosphatase activity.
outline_action: Search for methodological papers or consensus guidelines specifically addressing absolute quantification of short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) in human serum or tumor tissue. Investigate whether standardized LC-MS/MS or NMR protocols exist for free inosine measurement in serum or TME. Look for review articles or consortium statements (e.g., Metabolomics Society) that define reference methods for these specific metabolites in clinical oncology contexts.
remaining_gap: This material does not establish a standardized measurement method for free inosine or short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) in serum or the tumor microenvironment (TME). The study focuses on intracellular nucleotides in blood cells rather than absolute concentrations (μM or ng/mL) in serum or tissue. No consensus guidelines or widely adopted protocols for the specific metabolites and matrices requested in the gap (SCFAs, serum/TME inosine) are provided. The success criterion for finding consensus guidelines or widely adopted methodological papers for these specific targets remains open.
useful_material: This study developed and validated an LC-MS/MS method for quantifying adenosine, guanosine, and inosine nucleotides (mono- and triphosphate forms) in human peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs), red blood cells (RBCs), and dried blood spots (DBS). The authors reported linearity ranges (e.g., 0.25–50 pmol/sample for inosine triphosphate), intraassay and interassay precision (%CV within 1.7 to 16%), and accuracy (%deviation within −11.5 to 14.7%). The method involved solid-phase extraction followed by dephosphorylation to molar equivalent nucleosides. The study identified specific stability issues, noting that triphosphate levels in DBS were approximately 26% lower compared to paired RBC lysates due to hydrolysis during drying/storage. It also highlighted environmental contamination as a critical factor for low-abundance nucleotides like ITP, requiring strict controls and adjusted lower limits of quantification.
